original_test_intent: Validate creation, authentication, privilege/password modification and one-failure lockout for three BMC user roles under this row's independent source identity.
original_method: Capture the account and lockout-policy baseline; provision three approved temporary identities at the stated roles; establish fresh authenticated sessions and role boundaries; apply owner-defined privilege/password changes and repeat the checks; set the failed-attempt threshold to one, make one intentional bad authentication against a disposable identity, verify subsequent denial and recovery; restore policy and remove all test identities.
manual_activity: The security owner supplies the intended privilege transitions, safe allowed/denied probes and protected credentials; an operator authorizes each mutation, guards break-glass access and owns recovery and the final verdict.
required_inputs: Exact SUT/BMC and supported account-management interface
Approved edited privilege destination for every identity
Safe positive and negative permission probes per role
safety_requirements: Do not alter production, service or recovery identities
Keep passwords, hashes, tokens and session material out of commands and evidence
Prove independent recovery before changing lockout policy
Use fresh sessions when assessing new passwords and privileges
Issue exactly one intentional failed authentication to the disposable subject
Stop on unexpected privilege, lockout spread or recovery loss
Restore the threshold and remove or disable all temporary identities
agent_execution_scope: Operate only on approved temporary identities
Perform bounded login and safe authorization checks
Read lockout state, restore policy and clean up
Return evidence without assigning PASS, FAIL or BLOCKED
engineer_actions: Approve unique identities and initial/edited privilege matrix
Provide secrets through a protected mechanism
Maintain independent recovery and confirm cleanup
Resolve any access incident and decide PASS, FAIL or BLOCKED

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The proposed account inventories observe provisioning at most; they cannot demonstrate authenticated access, effective privileges, password rotation or threshold-one lockout.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use the supported account interface and isolated clients to execute the approved three-identity lifecycle, then the single-attempt lockout transaction, with baseline restoration and complete deletion/disablement evidence.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The three named roles, edit/password stage, threshold 1, one wrong attempt and 20/20-minute estimates are retained; unspecified edit destinations remain required owner inputs.

modernized_recommendation.status: ROW-BOUND THREE-IDENTITY ACCESS AND LOCKOUT TRANSACTION
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Record separate transaction IDs for each temporary account and for the lockout subject, pairing every mutation with readback and a fresh-session behavioral oracle; bind all artifacts to row 1588/code 00858.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Makes the unstated privilege matrix, safe authorization probes, secret handling, recovery and cleanup explicit without changing the source checkpoints.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Account enumeration alone cannot prove credential validity, effective authorization after edits or the lockout transition.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: A one-attempt policy leaves no retry margin; duplicate-looking neighboring source rows also create an audit risk if identity-specific evidence is reused without an approved execution-level deduplication decision.

project_override_considerations: The Project must specify edited privileges, safe boundary probes and whether later execution may deliberately reuse a controlled run; review counting and source evidence remain independently traceable for row 1588 regardless.
expected_evidence: Row-1588-bound SUT/BMC identity, approval, redacted account/policy baseline and recovery proof
Creation/readback and fresh authenticated session for each stated role
Allowed/denied authorization evidence for each initial role
Explicit privilege/password mutations plus new fresh-session and boundary results
Threshold-one readback, exactly one failed authentication, subsequent correct-credential denial and documented unlock result
Restored policy, removed/disabled temporary identities, intact break-glass path, preserved audit/SEL artifacts and engineer-owned verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Procedure and Criteria agree on provisioning, login, edit and lockout checkpoints. Unspecified edited roles and cleanup are required readiness details rather than contradictory source instructions.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Normal project inputs can resolve identity names, privilege transitions, secret custody, supported APIs and recovery; no source-level ambiguity prevents a safe controlled plan.

review_improvement: Provides identity-specific traceability and behavioral oracles for every account state transition while preventing the adjacent equal-text row from silently satisfying this record.
independent_technical_reasoning: The decisive lockout observation is not merely a flag or list entry: after one known bad attempt, a fresh correct credential must be refused according to the documented threshold state, and recovery must be independently demonstrated. Authentication and authorization must likewise be tested after, not inferred from, each account mutation.
